title: Largest Water Container
statement:
Choose two vertical walls so the rectangle between them holds as much area as possible.

Contract
- `heights` is non-null and may be empty; each value is a non-negative `int`, and wall i stands at x-coordinate i.
- Picking walls i < j encloses an area of `min(heights[i], heights[j]) * (j - i)`. Return the largest area over all pairs, or `0` when there are fewer than two walls.
- The area can exceed the `int` range, so the result is a `long`. Do not mutate `heights`.

Examples
- `maxArea(new int[]{1, 5, 2, 6, 3})` returns `10`, from the walls of height 5 and 6.
- `maxArea(new int[]{4, 4})` returns `4`.
- `maxArea(new int[]{7})` returns `0`.
hints: Start with the widest pair of walls, then ask which wall limits the area.
Moving the taller wall inward can never help because the shorter wall still caps the height while the width shrinks.
Keep two pointers at the ends, record the area, and move the pointer at the shorter wall. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the number of walls.
inputSyntax: Input: the wall heights, for example: [1, 5, 2, 6, 3]
